extraction.name: LAMBADA dataset
extraction.description: LAMBADA (LAnguage Modeling Broadened to Account for Discourse Aspects) is a dataset designed to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding through a word prediction task. It consists of narrative passages where human subjects can guess the last word if exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word. To succeed on LAMBADA, computational models must rely on broader discourse context rather than just local context. The dataset is proposed as a challenging test set to encourage the development of new models capable of genuine understanding of broad context in natural language text.
extraction.creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LAMBADA passages are composed of a context (on average 4.6 sentences) and a target sentence, with the task being to guess the last word of the target sentence. The data is sourced from the Book Corpus (Zhu et al., 2015), specifically from unpublished novels to minimize the use of general world knowledge. Novels were divided into training and development+testing partitions. Passages were initially filtered by a combination of four language models (RNN, 4-gram, feed-forward) to exclude those where the target word had a probability >= 0.00175, as these were considered easy for standard models. A random sample of the remaining passages was then evaluated by human subjects via CrowdFlower in three steps: 1) one subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage; 2) if correct, a second subject guessed based on the whole passage; 3) if also correct, more subjects (up to 10) tried to guess based on the target sentence only. Passages were added to LAMBADA if two consecutive subjects correctly guessed the word from the whole passage, and no subject (out of ten, with 3 guesses each) could guess it from the last sentence alone.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The LAMBADA data comes from the Book Corpus (Zhu et al., 2015), which contains unpublished novels.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Passages were filtered based on their predictability by a combination of four language models (RNN, 4-gram, feed-forward). Any passage whose target word had a probability >= 0.00175 according to any of these models was excluded. Further filtering was performed by human subjects to ensure the target word was guessable from broad context but not local context.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The Book Corpus underwent duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material with a stop word list. Novels were randomly divided into equally-sized training and development+testing partitions. Passages were extracted from the development+testing partition. Passages were filtered by language models to remove those easily guessable by local context. Human evaluation steps on CrowdFlower further filtered passages to ensure they met the criteria of being guessable from broad context but not local context.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human subjects on CrowdFlower were presented with passages and asked to guess the last word. In the first two steps, subjects were given the whole passage (context + target sentence) and asked to guess the target word. In the third step, subjects were given only the target sentence and asked to guess the target word. The 'annotation' process was a filtering step: passages were included in LAMBADA only if two different subjects correctly guessed the target word from the whole passage, and up to ten different subjects failed to guess the target word from the target sentence alone (even with 3 guesses each). The target word itself served as the 'label' that humans were attempting to predict.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The criteria for passage inclusion were very strict: two consecutive subjects were required to exactly match the missing word when given the whole passage, and no subject (out of ten) was able to provide it based on local context only, even when given 3 guesses. The authors opted for a strict 'hit-or-miss' approach, keeping only items that could be unambiguously determined by human subjects, rather than including passages where broad-context subjects provided plausible or synonymous continuations, due to the practical and methodological challenges of determining the fit of alternative answers for a dataset of this scale.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: For each passage, at least two human subjects guessed the target word based on the whole passage. Up to ten human subjects (each allowed 3 guesses) attempted to guess the target word based on the target sentence only.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to announce a public competition based on the LAMBADA data. The development set and training corpus are available for download. The test set will be made available at the time of the competition.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Proper nouns are hugely over-represented in LAMBADA (48%) compared to their distribution in the input data, while other categories like common nouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs are under-represented. LAMBADA items also contain quoted direct speech significantly more often (71%) than the overall input items (61%).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Cost considerations precluded the use of more subjects at stage 1 of the human evaluation, which could have improved the quality of filtering at that step. The strict 'perfect-match' approach for human annotation, requiring exact word matches, might exclude passages where plausible or synonymous continuations could also fit well. The dataset is designed to challenge language models with harder-than-average examples where broad context understanding is crucial, meaning standard language models are bound to fail on it by design due to the initial filtering process. This implies the dataset is not representative of average language modeling tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The LAMBADA dataset is intended for evaluating the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task. It serves as a challenging test set and benchmark to encourage the development of new models capable of genuine understanding of broad context in natural language text. The training partition of the Book Corpus is provided for training models to be tested on LAMBADA. The development data can be used to fine-tune models to the specifics of the LAMBADA passages. The dataset is justified as a tool to evaluate general-purpose models in terms of how they fare on broad-context understanding, rather than as a resource to develop ad-hoc models only meant to predict the final word in LAMBADA-specific passages.
